en.askTitle: Enter your own dates, pensions and savings and get a rent-first trial plan for Penang
en.runTitle: Retired British couple, Penang from late 2027: GBP 3,400 a month and GBP 220,000 saved

fields.label: Trial dates
fields.value: From late 2027, for most of the year

fields.label: Net pensions, by scheme
fields.value: Combined pensions of GBP 3,400 a month

fields.label: Protected medical reserve
fields.placeholder: e.g. GBP 30,000 kept aside for medical costs

fields.label: Areas
fields.value: Tanjung Bungah or Gurney (2–3 bedroom condo)

fields.label: Rent, insurance and GBP/MYR to stress-test
fields.placeholder: e.g. rent up to RM4,500, insurance £3,000 a year, 5.4 MYR per GBP

en.template: Help us plan a genuine Penang trial for {dates}. We are British retirees aged {ages}, with net pensions {pensions}, savings {savings} and protected medical reserve {reserve}. Compare lawful short-stay options in {areas}, stress-test {stress}, and list the medical, tax and residence questions to resolve. Keep rent-first as the starting point; assess MM2H only if we want to own and can fund the full cash peak. Ask before contacting anyone, sharing documents, applying or paying.

phases.title: Read the official Malaysian visa rules, Penang hospital prices and UK pension rules
phases.note: Residence scheme, hospitals, insurer, State Pension, tax treaty, NHS
phases.judgment: Where official sources disagreed, it recorded both versions instead of picking one: the annual-stay rule for over-50s and when the fixed deposit can be withdrawn. It also wrote down what it could not confirm, such as Penang’s own minimum and the rules for late 2027.

phases.title: Build the guide and the source log with every calculation shown
phases.note: Recommendation, requirements table, healthcare, pension and tax, rent examples, monthly budget
phases.judgment: The insurance and tax sections stay cautious: no insurance premium was quoted because none was found, and the guide warns against promising exemption from both UK and Malaysian tax at once. The monthly budget of RM14,130 (£2,616.67) is stated with its assumed exchange rate and costs.

phases.title: Independent check of claims and arithmetic, plus desktop and phone layout review
phases.judgment: The independent reviewer re-ran 90 numeric checks and all passed. It still flagged two wordings that sounded firmer than the sources, a fee called a “maximum” and a rent listing implied to run a year, as items to fix.

workers: Read Malaysia’s official My Second Home rules and fees (deposits, property, age and stay rules) and the DE Rantau pass
Collected Penang private-hospital prices, over-65 insurance evidence, NHS access, State Pension rules and the UK tax treatment of teacher pensions
Independently recomputed every money figure and checked the guide’s claims against the source list
